title: Supported finite-stage local systems do not detect the coefficient-topology scalar-unit defect
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers let
$$C(S)=\{f\in C(S,\Omega):f(S)\subset E\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset\Omega\},\qquad B(S)=C(S,\Omega).$$
These are the coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $C_T=p_T^*C$, $B_T=p_T^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $c_T:C_T\to B_T$ be induced by inclusion. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $J_X=B_X\otimes^L_{C_X}-$ and $U_X=\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}$, and let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to U_XJ_X$ be their derived adjunction unit [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], represented on a K-flat resolution by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$.

Choose two constructible locally closed immersions $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Define $a_!=i_*j_!$ after factoring $a=i\circ j$ into an open immersion into its closure followed by the closed immersion, and likewise for $b$, using the exact coefficient-module functors of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Choose finite intermediate fields $E,F\subset\Omega$, and lisse modules $L$ over $A_{E,S}=p_S^*C(-,E)$ and $M$ over $A_{F,T}=p_T^*C(-,F)$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], with the restricted norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Set
$$G=a_!\bigl(C_S\otimes^L_{A_{E,S}}L[0]\bigr),\qquad H=b_!\bigl(C_T\otimes^L_{A_{F,T}}M[0]\bigr).$$
For every distinguished triangle $H\xrightarrow{\eta_H}U_XJ_XH\to Q_H\to H[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category] and every integer $n$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_X})}(G,Q_H[n])=0.$$
Both supports, both finite fields and both local systems vary independently. Empty supports and rank-zero local systems are included. This is a statement only about these two finite-stage supported local systems and the specified scalar unit; it imposes no flatness on $c_X$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison input: supported finite-stage scalar-unit defect vanishing. Exact literature proof WANTED; HRS Lemma 7.9 concerns the colimit coefficient ring only.

proof.text: Pass to the small-site section-ring model using [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] and [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. The first identifies the specified derived tensors and exact open extension; closed internal Homs are identified by uniqueness of their right adjunctions. The second identifies scalar extension/restriction AND their actual units, including $v\mapsto1\otimes v$; thus this passage does not change the triangle in the assertion. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and itself); hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open in $X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Closed subschemes are Noetherian too: on a Noetherian affine their rings are quotients, whose ascending chains of ideals lift to chains of ideals upstairs, and closed subsets of a Noetherian space are quasi-compact. These observations apply also to the closures used to define $a_!,b_!$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; module models and quasi-compactness checks.

proof.text: Take the finite compositum $E_0=EF\subset\Omega$ by [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions], and write $A_V=A_{E_0,V}$. Extend $L,M$ on their respective supports to $L_0=A_S\otimes_{A_{E,S}}L$ and $M_0=A_T\otimes_{A_{F,T}}M$. These are ordinary degree-zero modules: finite-field scalar extension is exact by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]. They are lisse: pull back to the covers trivializing $L,M$; [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] identifies the pullbacks of these tensors with the tensors of the pullbacks, hence with $A^r,A^s$. Define $K=(a_!L_0)[0]$, $N=(b_!M_0)[0]$ in $D(A_X)$. They are bounded constructible by [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-lisse-extension-constructible], since $X$ is Noetherian. The two supports and ranks have not been identified.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; one common finite coefficient field; finite models.

proof.text: Scalar extension along each coefficient map used here commutes with $a_!$ and $b_!$. For their open factors this is [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], with the identity geometric map and the given change of rings. For the closed factors use [lem-sfb-closed-supported-scalar-comparison] with inverse-image comparisons [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Its unbounded-calculus hypothesis follows from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] and [lem-sfb-exact-open-closed-unbounded-calculus]: all four sheaf functors are exact; the open unit and closed counit are isomorphisms; the mixed restrictions are zero by extension by zero and disjoint supports. Applying the first recollement triangle to a degree-zero sheaf gives the required short exact sequence $0\to j_!j^*M\to M\to i_*i^*M\to0$. Complements are quasi-compact by step 1. Thus the cited unbounded calculus applies, without assuming that the scalar extensions are bounded or flat. The resulting closed comparison is linear over the new coefficient ring, with the precise counit normalization of that node.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; normalized scalar extension across supports.

proof.text: For $R=C_X,B_X$ put $S_R(V)=R\otimes_{A_X}^L V$. Apply step 3 first to $E\to E_0\to C$ on $S$, and to $F\to E_0\to C$ on $T$. The scalar reassociations of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] give $G\simeq S_CK$, $H\simeq S_CN$. Applying the same reassociation to $A_X\to C_X\to B_X$ gives $J_XG\simeq S_BK$, $J_XH\simeq S_BN$. All identifications are natural, and the cited reassociation takes successive scalar units to the direct unit, by $(v\otimes z)\otimes w\mapsto v\otimes c(z)w$. We may therefore make these identifications when computing the actual scalar-extension map on morphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; identify the supported objects and their scalar units.

proof.text: Put $D=R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K,N)$. The predicate comparison [lem-sfb-adic-constructibility-predicate-comparison] for the field $E_0$ on the Noetherian $X$ shows that $K,N$ are bounded constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense. So $D$ is bounded constructible in that sense by [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves], applied to $E_0$ in the standing setting. By the same comparison $D$ also has finite constant local models. The complex $K$ has the internal filtered-colimit continuity property of [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity]: $X$ is Noetherian and $K$ has the finite constant local model from step 2. Since $N$ is degree zero, it is bounded below. Consequently [lem-sfb-qlbar-internal-hom-coefficient-comparison] gives the evaluation-transpose isomorphism $\phi_C:S_CD\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{C_X}(S_CK,S_CN)$. Independently, [lem-sfb-norm-algcl-internal-hom-base-change] gives the evaluation-transpose isomorphism $\phi_B:S_BD\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(S_BK,S_BN)$. This second input is about the norm coefficient ring, so it is not inferred from the colimit-coefficient result.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; internal-Hom comparisons, with each coefficient topology distinguished.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-norm-algcl-cohomology-topology-comparison] to the bounded constructible $A_X$-complex $D$ from step 5. It makes the actual map $R\Gamma(m_D):R\Gamma(S_CD)\to R\Gamma(S_BD)$ invertible. Under $\phi_C,\phi_B$ this is the morphism on derived global Hom induced by $J_X$. Indeed both evaluation transposes are scalar extension of the same evaluation $D\otimes_{A_X}^L K\to N$. Reassociating balanced tensors, their evaluations after $c_X$ agree: both are $B_X\otimes_{A_X}^L(D\otimes_{A_X}^L K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}S_BN$. The defining tensor/internal-Hom adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] makes the transpose unique. Thus this equality identifies the actual map, including its naturality in arrows, rather than merely identifying its endpoints. Derived global sections of a $C_X$- or $B_X$-complex agree with those of its restriction to $A_X$: by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] applied to $A_X\to R$ and the unit $R$ itself, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(R,M[n])=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_X)}(A_X,M[n])$. Taking degree-$n$ cohomology and using [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] yields a bijection $u\mapsto J_Xu$ from $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C_X)}(G,H[n])$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_X)}(J_XG,J_XH[n])$ for every integer $n$. The module equivalences in step 1 preserve these constructions and underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; global comparison and evaluation identify its actual map.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] for $c_X:C_X\to B_X$. The right adjoint is exact restriction, and the normalized derived unit is exactly the one in the statement. The adjunction sends $J_Xu:J_XG\to J_XH[n]$ to $U_XJ_Xu\circ\eta_G=\eta_{H[n]}\circ u$ by naturality of the unit. Since these exact derived functors and their units commute with shifts, this is $\eta_H[n]\circ u$. Composing with the bijections from step 6 therefore shows that the maps $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H[n])\xrightarrow{\eta_H[n]\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(G,U_XJ_XH[n])$ are bijections for all integers $n$. This step uses no flatness of $c_X$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; adjunction transfers the comparison to the specified unit.

proof.text: Let the triangle in the assertion be arbitrary and let $q:G\to Q_H[n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] applied also to the shifted and rotated distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category], its boundary $dq:G\to H[n+1]$ is killed by $\eta_H[n+1]$. Step 7 makes that map on Hom injective, so $dq=0$. Exactness at $Q_H[n]$ gives $q=vh$ for some $h:G\to U_XJ_XH[n]$. Surjectivity in step 7 writes $h=\eta_H[n]u$; consecutive triangle arrows compose to zero, so $q=v\eta_H[n]u=0$. Thus every element of the asserted Hom group is zero. Nothing depended on a chosen cone, a nonempty support, a positive rank, or a relation between $S,T$ or $E,F$, so the asserted edge cases are included.
